281 void
282 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseLambdaExpression(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
283  {
284  SgLambdaExp* lambdaExp = isSgLambdaExp(expr);
285  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaExp);
286 
287 #if 0
288  printf ("In unparseLambdaExpression(expr = %p = %s) \n",expr,expr->class_name().c_str());
289 #endif
290 
291  // Liao, 7/1/2016
292  // To workaround some wrong AST generated from RAJA LULESH code
293  // we clear skip base type flag of unparse_info
294  if (info.SkipBaseType())
295  {
296  // DQ (4/7/2018): cleanup output spew (review with Liao).
297  // cout<<"Warning in Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseLambdaExpression(). Unparse_Info has skipBaseType() set. Unset it now."<<endl;
298  // ROSE_ASSERT(false);
299 
300  info.unset_SkipBaseType ();
301  }
302 
303  curprint(" [");
304  // if '=' or '&' exists
305  bool hasCaptureCharacter = false;
306  int commaCounter = 0;
307 
308  // schroder3 (2016-08-23): Do not print "&" AND "=" (because "[&=](){}" is ill-formed):
309  if (lambdaExp->get_capture_default() == true) {
310  if (lambdaExp->get_default_is_by_reference() == true) {
311  curprint("&");
312  }
313  else {
314  curprint("=");
315  }
316  hasCaptureCharacter = true;
317  }
318  else {
319  // schroder3 (2016-08-23): Consistency check: If there is no capture default then there should be no
320  // by-reference-capture default:
321  ROSE_ASSERT(!lambdaExp->get_default_is_by_reference());
322  }
323 
324 
325 
326  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaExp->get_lambda_capture_list());
327  size_t bound = lambdaExp->get_lambda_capture_list()->get_capture_list().size();
328  for (size_t i = 0; i < bound; i++)
329  {
330  SgLambdaCapture* lambdaCapture = lambdaExp->get_lambda_capture_list()->get_capture_list()[i];
331  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaCapture);
332 
333  // schroder3 (2016-08-23): Do not print implicit captures because this generates ill-formed code if
334  // there is a capture default (C++ standard section [expr.prim.lambda] point 8) (g++ allows this in
335  // non-pedantic mode, clang++ does not). Example: do not transform "int i; [&](){i;};" to ill-formed
336  // "int i; [&, &i](){i;}"). In addition, this change prevents the printing of "&this" (which is
337  // ill-formed too) when "this" is implicitly captured.
338  if (!lambdaCapture->get_implicit() && lambdaCapture->get_capture_variable() != NULL)
339  {
340 
341  // Liao 6/24/2016, we output ",item" when
342  // When not output , : first comma and there is no previous = or & character
343  if (commaCounter == 0) // look backwards one identifier
344  {
345  if (hasCaptureCharacter)
346  curprint(",");
347  commaCounter ++;
348  }
349  else {
350  curprint(",");
351  }
352 
353  SgExpression * capt_var_expr = lambdaCapture->get_capture_variable();
354  ASSERT_not_null(capt_var_expr);
355 
356  if (isSgThisExp(capt_var_expr)) {
357  if (lambdaCapture->get_capture_by_reference() == false) {
358  curprint("*");
359  }
360  curprint("this");
361  } else {
362  if (lambdaCapture->get_capture_by_reference() == true)
363  {
364  curprint("&");
365  }
366  unp->u_exprStmt->unparseExpression(capt_var_expr,info);
367  }
368 
369  }
370  }
371  curprint("] ");
372 
373  SgFunctionDeclaration* lambdaFunction = lambdaExp->get_lambda_function();
374  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction);
375  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration());
376  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction->get_definingDeclaration());
377 
378  if (lambdaFunction->get_functionModifier().isCudaHost()) {
379  curprint("__host__ ");
380  }
381  if (lambdaFunction->get_functionModifier().isCudaKernel()) {
382  curprint("__global__ ");
383  }
384  if (lambdaFunction->get_functionModifier().isCudaDevice()) {
385  curprint("__device__ ");
386  }
387 
388  if (lambdaExp->get_has_parameter_decl() == true)
389  {
390  // Output the function parameters
391  curprint("(");
392  unparseFunctionArgs(lambdaFunction,info);
393  curprint(")");
394  }
395 
396  if (lambdaExp->get_is_mutable() == true)
397  {
398  curprint(" mutable ");
399  }
400 
401  if (lambdaExp->get_explicit_return_type() == true)
402  {
403  curprint(" -> ");
404  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction);
405  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction->get_type());
406  SgType* returnType = lambdaFunction->get_type()->get_return_type();
407  ASSERT_not_null(returnType);
408  unp->u_type->unparseType(returnType,info);
409  }
410 
411  // Use a new SgUnparse_Info object to support supression of the SgThisExp where compiler generated.
412  // This is required because the function is internally a member function but can't explicitly refer
413  // to a "this" expression.
414  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
415  ninfo.set_supressImplicitThisOperator();
416 
417  // DQ (2/19/2018): Need to unset the support to skip the function definitions so that the unparsing of the block will allow comments and CPP directives to be output.
418  ninfo.unset_SkipEnumDefinition();
419  ninfo.unset_SkipClassDefinition();
420  ninfo.unset_SkipFunctionDefinition();
421 
422  // Output the function definition
423  ASSERT_not_null(lambdaFunction->get_definition());
424  unparseStatement(lambdaFunction->get_definition()->get_body(), ninfo);
425  }

507 void
508 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTemplateFunctionName(SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl* templateInstantiationFunctionDeclaration, SgUnparse_Info& info)
509  {
510  // DQ (6/21/2011): Generated this function from refactored call to unparseTemplateArgumentList
511  ASSERT_not_null(templateInstantiationFunctionDeclaration);
512 
513  unp->u_exprStmt->curprint(templateInstantiationFunctionDeclaration->get_templateName().str());
514 
515  bool unparseTemplateArguments = templateInstantiationFunctionDeclaration->get_template_argument_list_is_explicit();
516 
517  // DQ (6/29/2013): Use the information recorded in the AST as to if this function has been used with
518  // template arguments in the original code. If so then we always unparse the template arguments, if
519  // not then we never unparse the template arguments. See test2013_242.C for an example of where this
520  // is significant in the generated code. Note that this goes a long way toward making the generated
521  // code look more like the original input code (where before we have always unparsed template arguments
522  // resulting in some very long function calls in the generated code). Note that if some template
523  // arguments are specified and some are not then control over not unparsing template arguments that
524  // where not explicit in the original code will be handled seperately in the near future (in the
525  // SgTemplateArgument IR nodes).
526  if (unparseTemplateArguments == true)
527  {
528  unparseTemplateArgumentList(templateInstantiationFunctionDeclaration->get_templateArguments(),info);
529  }
530  }

532 
533 void
534 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTemplateMemberFunctionName(SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl* templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration, SgUnparse_Info& info)
535  {
536  // DQ (5/25/2013): Generated this function to match that of unparseTemplateFunctionName().
537  ASSERT_not_null(templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration);
538 
539  string function_name = templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_templateName();
540 
541  // DQ (6/15/2013): Now that we have fixed template handling for member function name output in member
542  // function reference handling, we have to make sure that if handle cases where the operator name
543  // (for a conversion operator) has template arguments. We have to make sure we don't ouput names
544  // that contain "<<" or ">>" (since these need an extra space to be unparsed in C++, somthing fixed
545  // in C++11, as I recall).
546  // This code is translating "s >> len;" to "s > > len;" in test2013_97.C.
547  if (function_name != "operator>>")
548  {
549  // DQ (11/18/2012): Process the function name to remove any cases of ">>" from template names.
550  string targetString = ">>";
551  string replacementString = "> >";
552  size_t found = function_name.find(targetString);
553  while (found != string::npos)
554  {
555  function_name.replace(found,targetString.length(),replacementString);
556  found = function_name.find(targetString);
557  }
558  }
559 
560  unp->u_exprStmt->curprint(function_name);
561 
562  // DQ (5/26/2013): test2013_194.C demonstrates that we need to drop the template argument list for the case of a constructor (I think).
563  // I think that this applies to constructors, destructors, and conversion operators, but I am not sure...
564  bool isConstructor = templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_specialFunctionModifier().isConstructor();
565  bool isDestructor = templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_specialFunctionModifier().isDestructor();
566  bool isConversionOperator = templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_specialFunctionModifier().isConversion();
567 
568  // DQ (5/26/2013): Output output the template argument list when this is not a constructor, destructor, or conversion operator.
569  bool skipTemplateArgumentList = (isConstructor == true || isDestructor == true || isConversionOperator == true);
570 
571  // DQ (6/29/2013): Use the information recorded in the AST as to if this function has been used with
572  // template arguments in the original code. See note in unparseTemplateFunctionName().
573  bool unparseTemplateArguments = templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_template_argument_list_is_explicit();
574  if (unparseTemplateArguments == false)
575  {
576  skipTemplateArgumentList = true;
577  }
578 
579  if (skipTemplateArgumentList == false)
580  {
581  unparseTemplateArgumentList(templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_templateArguments(),info);
582  }
583  }

586 
587 void SgTemplateArgument::outputTemplateArgument(bool & skip_unparsing, bool & stop_unparsing) {
588 
589 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
590  printf ("outputTemplateArgument(this = %p (%s)\n", this, this->class_name().c_str());
591  printf (" --- this->kind = %s \n", this->template_argument_kind().c_str());
592 #endif
593 
594  ROSE_ASSERT(!skip_unparsing);
595  ROSE_ASSERT(!stop_unparsing);
596 
597  bool isExplicitlySpecified = this->get_explicitlySpecified();
598 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
599  printf (" --- isExplicitlySpecified = %s \n", isExplicitlySpecified ? "true" : "false");
600 #endif
601 
602  bool isPackElement = this->get_is_pack_element();
603 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
604  printf (" --- isPackElement = %s \n", isPackElement ? "true" : "false");
605 #endif
606 
607  SgNode * parentOfTemplateArgument = this->get_parent();
608  ASSERT_not_null(parentOfTemplateArgument);
609  SgClassDeclaration * xdecl = isSgClassDeclaration(parentOfTemplateArgument);
610  if (xdecl != NULL) {
611 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
612  printf (" !!! template argument for a class template => isExplicitlySpecified == true\n");
613 #endif
614  isExplicitlySpecified = true;
615  }
616 
617  if (isPackElement && isExplicitlySpecified) {
618 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
619  printf (" !!! isPackElement && isExplicitlySpecified => isPackElement == false\n");
620 #endif
621  isPackElement = false;
622  }
623 
624  bool isAnonymousClass = this->isTemplateArgumentFromAnonymousClass();
625 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
626  printf (" --- isAnonymousClass = %s \n", isAnonymousClass ? "true" : "false");
627 #endif
628 
629  bool isAssociatedWithLambdaExp = false;
630  if (this->get_argumentType() == SgTemplateArgument::type_argument) {
631  SgClassType * xtype = isSgClassType(this->get_type());
632  if (xtype != NULL) {
633 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
634  printf (" - xtype = %p (%s) = %s \n", xtype, xtype->class_name().c_str(), xtype->unparseToString().c_str());
635 #endif
636  SgDeclarationStatement * xdecl = xtype->get_declaration();
637  ASSERT_not_null(xdecl);
638 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
639  printf (" - xdecl = %p (%s)\n", xdecl, xdecl->class_name().c_str());
640 #endif
641  SgNode * pnode = xdecl->get_parent();
642 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
643  printf (" - pnode = %p (%s)\n", pnode, pnode ? pnode->class_name().c_str() : "");
644 #endif
645  SgLambdaExp * lambda_exp = isSgLambdaExp(pnode);
646  if (lambda_exp != NULL) {
647  isAssociatedWithLambdaExp = true;
648  }
649  }
650  }
651 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
652  printf (" --- isAssociatedWithLambdaExp = %s \n", isAssociatedWithLambdaExp ? "true" : "false");
653 #endif
654 
655  bool isPackExpansionStart = this->get_argumentType() == SgTemplateArgument::start_of_pack_expansion_argument;
656 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
657  printf (" --- isPackExpansionStart = %s \n", isPackExpansionStart ? "true" : "false");
658 #endif
659 
660  if ( isPackExpansionStart || isAnonymousClass || ( isPackElement && !isExplicitlySpecified ) ) {
661  skip_unparsing = true;
662  }
663 
664  if ( isAssociatedWithLambdaExp ) {
665  stop_unparsing = true;
666  }
667 #if DEBUG_OUTPUT_TEMPLATE_ARGUMENT
668  printf (" >>> skip_unparsing = %s \n", skip_unparsing ? "true" : "false");
669  printf (" >>> stop_unparsing = %s \n", stop_unparsing ? "true" : "false");
670 #endif
671 }

1354 void
1355 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparse_asm_operand_modifier(SgAsmOp::asm_operand_modifier_enum flags)
1356  {
1357  // Modifiers to asm operand strings. These are all machine independent.
1358  // Many of them do not make sense in asm() but are included anyway for
1359  // completeness. Note that these are bitmasks, and that
1360  // aom_input + aom_output == aom_modify.
1361 
1362  // e_invalid = 0x00, error
1363  // e_input = 0x01, no mod: input operand
1364  // e_output = 0x02, =: output operand
1365  // e_modify = 0x03, +: read-mod-write operand
1366  // e_earlyclobber = 0x04, &: modified early, cannot overlap inputs
1367  // e_commutative = 0x08, %: commutative with next operand
1368  // e_ignore_next = 0x10, *: ignore next letter as a register pref
1369  // e_ignore_till_comma = 0x20, #: ignore up to comma as a register pref
1370  // e_poor_choice = 0x40, ?: avoid choosing this
1371  // e_bad_choice = 0x80 !: really avoid choosing this
1372 
1373  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_invalid) curprint ( "error");
1374 
1375  // DQ (7/23/2006): The coding of these is a bit more complex, get it? :-)
1376  // if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_input) curprint ( "";
1377  // if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_output) curprint ( "=";
1378  // if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_modify) curprint ( "+";
1379 
1380  if ( ((flags & SgAsmOp::e_input) != 0) && ((flags & SgAsmOp::e_output) != 0) )
1381  {
1382  // This is how "modify" is coded!
1383 #if PRINT_DEVELOPER_WARNINGS
1384  printf ("This is how modify is coded \n");
1385 #endif
1386  // DQ (8/10/2006): Intel compiler can not handle the output of modifier for input operand:
1387  // error: an asm input operand may not have the '=' or '+' modifiers
1388  // curprint ( "+";
1389  // if ( string(BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH) != string("icpc") && (flags & SgAsmOp::e_output) )
1390  // if ( string(BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH) != string("icpc") )
1391  curprint ( "+");
1392  }
1393  else
1394  {
1395  // Only one of these are true
1396  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_output) curprint ( "=");
1397 
1398  // We need an exact match not a partial match!
1399 
1400 #if PRINT_DEVELOPER_WARNINGS
1401  printf ("We need an exact match not a partial match \n");
1402 #endif
1403  // DQ (8/10/2006): Intel compiler can not handle the output of modifier for input operand:
1404  // error: an asm input operand may not have the '=' or '+' modifiers
1405  // if ( string(BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH) != string("icpc") )
1406  {
1407  if ((flags & SgAsmOp::e_modify) == SgAsmOp::e_modify) curprint ( "+");
1408  }
1409  }
1410 
1411  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_earlyclobber) curprint ( "&");
1412  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_commutative) curprint ( "%");
1413  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_ignore_next) curprint ( "*");
1414  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_ignore_till_comma) curprint ( "#");
1415  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_poor_choice) curprint ( "?");
1416  if (flags & SgAsmOp::e_bad_choice) curprint ( "!");
1417  }

1419 void
1420 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseAsmOp (SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
1421  {
1422  // Just call unparse on the statement.
1423  SgAsmOp* asmOp = isSgAsmOp(expr);
1424  ASSERT_not_null(asmOp);
1425 
1426  // printf ("In unparseAsmOp(): asmOp->get_recordRawAsmOperandDescriptions() = %s \n",asmOp->get_recordRawAsmOperandDescriptions() ? "true" : "false");
1427 
1428  SgExpression* expression = asmOp->get_expression();
1429  ASSERT_not_null(expression);
1430 
1431  if (asmOp->get_name().empty() == false)
1432  {
1433  // This is symbolic name indicated for this operand (using the "[ <identifier> ]" syntax, if present).
1434  curprint ("[" + asmOp->get_name() + "] ");
1435  }
1436 
1437  curprint ( "\"");
1438  if (asmOp->get_recordRawAsmOperandDescriptions() == false)
1439  {
1440  // This is only set to non-invalid state when RECORD_RAW_ASM_OPERAND_DESCRIPTIONS == FALSE in EDG.
1441  unparse_asm_operand_modifier(asmOp->get_modifiers());
1442  curprint ( unparse_operand_constraint(asmOp->get_constraint()));
1443  }
1444  else
1445  {
1446  // The modifier is part of the constraint, and it is output in the constraintString when recordRawAsmOperandDescriptions() == true.
1447 #if 0
1448  printf ("asmOp->get_constraintString() = %s \n",asmOp->get_constraintString().c_str());
1449 #endif
1450  curprint ( asmOp->get_constraintString() );
1451  }
1452 
1453  // This is usually a SgVarRefExp
1454  curprint ( "\"");
1455  curprint ( " (");
1456  unparseExpression(expression,info);
1457  curprint ( ")");
1458  }

1460 void
1461 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseStatementExpression (SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
1462  {
1463  // Just call unparse on the statement.
1464  SgStatementExpression* statementExpression = isSgStatementExpression(expr);
1465  ASSERT_not_null(statementExpression);
1466  SgStatement* statement = statementExpression->get_statement();
1467  ASSERT_not_null(statement);
1468 
1469  // DQ (10/7/2006): Even if we are in a conditional the statements appearing in the
1470  // statement expression must have ";" output (here we have to turn off the flags
1471  // to both SkipSemiColon and inConditional). See test2006_148.C for an example.
1472  SgUnparse_Info info2(info);
1473  info2.unset_SkipSemiColon();
1474  info2.unset_inConditional();
1475 
1476  // Expressions are another place where a class definition should NEVER be unparsed
1477  // DQ (5/23/2007): Note that statement expressions can have class definition
1478  // (so they are exceptions, see test2007_51.C).
1479  info2.unset_SkipClassDefinition();
1480 
1481  // DQ (1/9/2014): We have to make the handling of enum definitions consistant with that of class definitions.
1482  info2.unset_SkipEnumDefinition();
1483 
1484  curprint ( "(");
1485  unparseStatement(statement,info2);
1486  curprint ( ")");
1487  }

1489 void
1490 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseUnaryOperator(SgExpression* expr, const char* op, SgUnparse_Info & info)
1491  {
1492  //
1493  // Flag to keep to original state of the "this" option
1494  //
1495  bool orig_this_opt = unp->opt.get_this_opt();
1496  SgUnparse_Info newinfo(info);
1497  newinfo.set_operator_name(op);
1498  //
1499  // If the "this" option was originally false, then we shouldn't print "this."
1500  // however, this only applies when the "this" is part of a binary expression.
1501  // In the unary case, we must print "this," otherwise a syntax error will be
1502  // produced. (i.e. *this)
1503  //
1504  if ( !orig_this_opt )
1505  unp->opt.set_this_opt(true);
1506 
1507 #if 0
1508  curprint ("\n /* Inside of unparseUnaryOperator(" + expr->class_name() + "," + op + ",SgUnparse_Info) */ \n");
1509 #endif
1510 
1511  unparseUnaryExpr(expr, newinfo);
1512 
1513  //
1514  // Now set the "this" option back to its original state
1515  //
1516  if( !orig_this_opt )
1517  unp->opt.set_this_opt(false);
1518  }

2461  // often we want to unparse the code as "a[i]" but there is a case were this is not possible
2462  // ("a->operator[](i)" is valid as is "(*a)[i]", but only if the operator-> is not defined for
2463  // the type of which "a" is a variable). So here we check the lhs of the parent of the curprintrent
2464  // expression so that we can detect this special case!
2465 
2466  // DQ (12/11/2004): We need to unparse the keyword "operator" in this special cases (see test2004_159.C)
2467  SgExpression* parentExpression = isSgExpression(expr->get_parent());
2468  ASSERT_not_null(parentExpression);
2469  SgDotExp* dotExpression = isSgDotExp(parentExpression);
2470  if (dotExpression != NULL)
2471  {
2472  SgExpression* lhs = dotExpression->get_lhs_operand();
2473  ASSERT_not_null(lhs);
2474  }
2475  }
2476  else
2477  {
2478 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2479  printf ("Case of unparsing a member function which is NOT short form of \"operator[]\" (i.e. \"[]\") funct_name = %s \n",func_name.c_str());
2480 #endif
2481  // Make sure that the member function name does not include "()" (this prevents "operator()()" from being output)
2482  if (func_name != "()")
2483  {
2484 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2485  printf ("Case of unparsing a member function which is NOT \"operator()\" \n");
2486  curprint ("/* Case of unparsing a member function which is NOT \"operator()\" */ \n");
2487 #endif
2488  // DQ (12/11/2004): Catch special case of "a.operator->();" and avoid unparsing it as "a->;" (illegal C++ code)
2489  // Get the parent SgFunctionCall so that we can check if it's parent was a SgDotExp with a valid rhs_operand!
2490  // if not then we have the case of "a.operator->();"
2491 
2492  // It might be that this could be a "->" instead of a "."
2493  ASSERT_not_null(mfunc_ref);
2494  SgDotExp *dotExpression = isSgDotExp (mfunc_ref->get_parent());
2495  SgArrowExp *arrowExpression = isSgArrowExp(mfunc_ref->get_parent());
2496 
2497  // Note that not all references to a member function are a function call.
2498  SgFunctionCallExp* functionCall = NULL;
2499  if (dotExpression != NULL)
2500  {
2501  functionCall = isSgFunctionCallExp(dotExpression->get_parent());
2502  }
2503  if (arrowExpression != NULL)
2504  {
2505  functionCall = isSgFunctionCallExp(arrowExpression->get_parent());
2506  }
2507 
2508 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2509  curprint (string("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): (functionCall != NULL) && (uses_operator_syntax == false) = ") + (((functionCall != NULL) && (uses_operator_syntax == false)) ? "true" : "false") + " */ \n");
2510  curprint (string("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): (functionCall != NULL) = ") + ((functionCall != NULL) ? "true" : "false") + " */ \n");
2511  curprint (string("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): uses_operator_syntax = ") + (uses_operator_syntax ? "true" : "false") + " */ \n");
2512 #endif
2513 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2514  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): functionCall = %p uses_operator_syntax = %s \n",functionCall,uses_operator_syntax ? "true" : "false");
2515 #endif
2516  if ( (functionCall != NULL) && (uses_operator_syntax == false) )
2517  {
2518  if ( unp->u_sage->isUnaryOperatorArrowSubtree(functionCall) == true )
2519  {
2520  // DQ (Dec, 2004): special (rare) case of .operator->() or ->operator->()
2521  // decided to handle these cases because they are amusing (C++ Trivia) :-).
2522  if (dotExpression != NULL)
2523  {
2524  curprint("operator->");
2525  }
2526  else
2527  {
2528  curprint("operator->");
2529  }
2530  }
2531  else
2532  {
2533  // DQ (2/9/2010): Fix for test2010_03.C
2534  // DQ (6/15/2013): The code for processing the function name when it contains template arguments that requires name qualification.
2535 
2536  // DQ (5/25/2013): Added support to unparse the template arguments seperately from the member function name (which should NOT
2537  // include the template arguments when unparsing). Note the the template arguments in the name are important for the generation
2538  // of mangled names for use in symbol tabls, but that we need to output the member function name and it's template arguments
2539  // seperately so that they name qulification can be computed and saved in the name qualification name maps.
2540 
2541  // Note that this code below is a copy of that from the support for unpasing the SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl (in function above).
2542 
2543  SgDeclarationStatement* declaration = mfd;
2544  ASSERT_not_null(declaration);
2545 
2546  // If this is a template then the name will include template arguments which require name qualification and the name
2547  // qualification will depend on where the name is referenced in the code. So we have generate the non-canonical name
2548  // with all possible qualifications and save it to be reused by the unparser when it unparses the tempated function name.
2549  SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl* templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl = isSgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl(declaration);
2550  if (templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl != NULL)
2551  {
2552  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().isFriend() == false)
2553  {
2554  unparseTemplateMemberFunctionName(templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl,info);
2555  }
2556  else
2557  {
2558  // This case supports test2004_77.C
2559 
2560  printf ("WARNING: In unparseMFuncRef(): No name qualification permitted in this case! (not clear if this case if important for unparseMFuncRef(), as it was for unparseFuncRef()) \n");
2561 
2562  // DQ (6/15/2013): I think this mod is required for test2010_03.C.
2563  curprint(" " + func_name + " ");
2564  }
2565  }
2566  else
2567  {
2568  // DQ (6/15/2013): I think this mod is required for test2010_03.C.
2569  curprint(" " + func_name + " ");
2570  }
2571  }
2572  }
2573  else
2574  {
2575  // If uses_operator_syntax == true, then we want to have the unparseMFuncRefSupport() NOT output the
2576  // operator name since it is best done by the binary operator handling (e.g. unparseBinaryExpr()).
2577  if ( uses_operator_syntax == false )
2578  {
2579 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2580  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name IS output \n");
2581  curprint("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name IS output */ \n");
2582 #endif
2583 
2584  // DQ (5/25/2013): Added support to unparse the template arguments seperately from the member function name (which should NOT
2585  // include the template arguments when unparsing). Note the the template arguments in the name are important for the generation
2586  // of mangled names for use in symbol tabls, but that we need to output the member function name and it's template arguments
2587  // seperately so that they name qulification can be computed and saved in the name qualification name maps.
2588 
2589  // Note that this code below is a copy of that from the support for unpasing the SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl (in function above).
2590  SgDeclarationStatement* declaration = mfd;
2591 
2592  // DQ (6/21/2011): Support for new name qualification (output of generated function name).
2593  ASSERT_not_null(declaration);
2594  // printf ("Inside of Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseFuncRef(): declaration = %p = %s \n",declaration,declaration->class_name().c_str());
2595  // If this is a template then the name will include template arguments which require name qualification and the name
2596  // qualification will depend on where the name is referenced in the code. So we have generate the non-canonical name
2597  // with all possible qualifications and save it to be reused by the unparser when it unparses the tempated function name.
2598  SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl* templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl = isSgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl(declaration);
2599  if (templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl != NULL)
2600  {
2601  if (declaration->get_declarationModifier().isFriend() == false)
2602  {
2603  unparseTemplateMemberFunctionName(templateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl,info);
2604  }
2605  else
2606  {
2607  // This case supports test2004_77.C
2608  printf ("WARNING: In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): No name qualification permitted in this case! (not clear if this case if important for unparseMFuncRef(), as it was for unparseFuncRef()) \n");
2609 
2610  curprint (func_name);
2611  }
2612  }
2613  else
2614  {
2615  curprint (func_name);
2616  }
2617  }
2618  else
2619  {
2620 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2621  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name is NOT output: full_function_name = %s \n",full_function_name.c_str());
2622  curprint("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name is NOT output */ \n");
2623 #endif
2624 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2625  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): mfd->get_args().size() = %" PRIuPTR " \n",mfd->get_args().size());
2626 #endif
2627  // DQ (11/17/2013): We need to distinguish between unary and binary overloaded operators (for member
2628  // functions a unary operator has zero arguments, and a binary operator has a single argument).
2629  bool is_unary_operator = (mfd->get_args().size() == 0);
2630 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2631  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): is_unary_operator = %s \n",is_unary_operator ? "true" : "false");
2632  // printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): is_compiler_generated = %s \n",is_compiler_generated ? "true" : "false");
2633 #endif
2634  // DQ (7/6/2014): If this is compiler generated then supress the output of the operator name.
2635  if (isPartOfArrowOperatorChain == false)
2636  {
2637  // DQ (7/5/2014): Adding operator-> as an additional special case.
2638  // These operators require special handling since they are prefix operators when unparsed using operator syntax.
2639  if ( (is_unary_operator == false) || (is_unary_operator == true && full_function_name != "operator*" && full_function_name != "operator&"))
2640  {
2641 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2642  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): not overloaded reference or dereference operator: function name IS output: func_name = %s \n",func_name.c_str());
2643  curprint("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): not overloaded reference or dereference operator: function name = " + func_name + " IS output */ \n");

2645  curprint(" " + func_name + " ");

2647  else
2648  {
2649 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2650  printf ("info.isPrefixOperator() = %s \n",info.isPrefixOperator() ? "true" : "false");
2651 #endif
2652  if (info.isPrefixOperator() == true)
2653  {
2654  curprint(" " + func_name + " ");
2655  }
2656  else
2657  {
2658 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2659  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name is NOT output for this operator: func_name = %s \n",func_name.c_str());
2660  curprint("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): function name is NOT output for this operator: func_name = " + func_name + " */ \n");

2665  else

2667 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2668  printf ("In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): case of isPartOfArrowOperatorChain == true: function name is NOT output for this operator: func_name = %s \n",func_name.c_str());
2669  curprint("/* In unparseMFuncRefSupport(): case of isPartOfArrowOperatorChain == true: function name is NOT output for this operator: func_name = " + func_name + " */ \n");

2682 
2683  // End of old code (not yet intended properly).
2684  }
2685 
2686 #if MFuncRefSupport_DEBUG
2687  printf ("Leaving unparseMFuncRefSupport \n");
2688  curprint ("\n/* leaving unparseMFuncRefSupport */ \n");

2693 // DQ (2/21/2019): Adding support to remove "\000" substrings from output strings in SgStringVal unparsing.
2694 template<typename T>
2695 void remove_substrings(basic_string<T>& s, const basic_string<T>& p)
2696  {
2697  typename basic_string<T>::size_type n = p.length();
2698 
2699 #if 0
2700  size_t string_size = s.length();
2701  for (size_t j = 0; j < string_size; j++)
2702  {
2703  int character_value = s[j];
2704  printf ("character_value = %d \n",character_value);
2705  }
2706 #endif
2707 
2708  for (typename basic_string<T>::size_type i = s.find(p); i != basic_string<T>::npos; i = s.find(p))
2709  {
2710 #if 0
2711  printf ("In remove_substrings: loop: i = %zu s = %s \n",i,s.c_str());
2712 #endif
2713  s.erase(i, n);
2714  }
2715 
2716 #if 0
2717  printf ("Leaving remove_substrings() \n");
2718 #endif
2719  }

2735 #ifndef CXX_IS_ROSE_CODE_GENERATION

2737  curprint("L");
2738  } else if (str_val->get_is16bitString()) {
2739  curprint("u");
2740  } else if (str_val->get_is32bitString()) {
2741  SgFile* file = TransformationSupport::getFile(str_val);

2744  curprint("U");

2746  curprint("L");
2747  }
2748  }
2749 
2750  std::string s;

2752  curprint("R");
2753  s = std::string("\"(") + str_val->get_value() + std::string(")\"");
2754  std::string p = "\\000";
2755  remove_substrings(s, p);
2756  } else {
2757  s = std::string("\"") + str_val->get_value() + std::string("\"");
2758  }
2759  curprint(s);
2760 #endif
2761  unp->u_sage->cur_set_linewrap(wrap);

2871 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseFloatVal(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
2872  {
2873  SgFloatVal* float_val = isSgFloatVal(expr);
2874  ASSERT_not_null(float_val);
2875 
2876 #if 0
2877  printf ("Inside of unparseFloatVal = %p \n",float_val);
2878  float_val->get_file_info()->display("unparseFloatVal");
2879 #endif
2880 
2881  // DQ (10/18/2005): Need to handle C code which cannot use C++ mechanism to specify
2882  // infinity, quiet NaN, and signaling NaN values. Note that we can't use the C++
2883  // interface since the input program, and thus the generated code, might not have
2884  // included the "limits" header file.
2885  float float_value = float_val->get_value();
2886 #if 0
2887  if (SageInterface::is_C_language() == true)
2888  {
2889  if (float_val->get_valueString() == "")
2890  {
2891  curprint ( tostring(float_val->get_value()));
2892  }
2893  else
2894  {
2895  curprint ( float_val->get_valueString());
2896  }
2897  }
2898  else
2899  {
2900  }
2901 #endif
2902 
2903  if (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity())
2904  {
2905  // printf ("Infinite value found as value in unparseFloatVal() \n");
2906  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()";
2907  curprint ( "__builtin_huge_valf()");
2908  }
2909  else
2910  {
2911  // Test for NaN value (famous test of to check for equality) or check for C++ definition of NaN.
2912  // We detect C99 and C "__NAN__" in EDG, but translate to backend specific builtin function.
2913  if ((float_value != float_value) || (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN()) )
2914  {
2915  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN()";
2916  curprint ( "__builtin_nanf (\"\")");
2917  }
2918  else
2919  {
2920  if (float_value == std::numeric_limits<float>::signaling_NaN())
2921  {
2922  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<float>::signaling_NaN()";
2923  curprint ( "__builtin_nansf (\"\")");
2924  }
2925  else
2926  {
2927  // typical case!
2928  // curprint ( float_val->get_value();
2929  // AS (11/08/2005) add support for values as string
2930  if (float_val->get_valueString() == "") {
2931  curprint ( tostring(float_value) );
2932  if (!info.get_user_defined_literal()) {
2933  curprint ( "L" );
2934  }
2935  } else {
2936  std::string strVal = float_val->get_valueString();
2937  if (info.get_user_defined_literal() && ( strVal.at(strVal.length() - 1) == 'f' || strVal.at(strVal.length() - 1) == 'F' ) ) {
2938  strVal = strVal.substr(0, strVal.length() - 1);
2939  }
2940  curprint (strVal);
2941  }
2942  }
2943  }
2944  }
2945  }

2999  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN()";
3000  curprint ( "__builtin_nan (\"\")");

3003  {
3004  if (double_value == std::numeric_limits<double>::signaling_NaN())

3013  // AS (11/08/2005) add support for values as string

3026 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseLongDoubleVal(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
3027  {
3028  SgLongDoubleVal* longdbl_val = isSgLongDoubleVal(expr);
3029  ASSERT_not_null(longdbl_val);
3030 
3031  // curprint ( longdbl_val->get_value();
3032 
3033  // DQ (10/18/2005): Need to handle C code which cannot use C++ mechanism to specify
3034  // infinity, quiet NaN, and signaling NaN values.
3035  long double longDouble_value = longdbl_val->get_value();
3036  if (longDouble_value == std::numeric_limits<long double>::infinity())
3037  {
3038  // printf ("Infinite value found as value in unparseFloatVal() \n");
3039  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<long double>::infinity()";
3040  curprint ( "__builtin_huge_vall()");
3041  }
3042  else
3043  {
3044  // Test for NaN value (famous test of to check for equality) or check for C++ definition of NaN.
3045  // We detect C99 and C "__NAN__" in EDG, but translate to backend specific builtin function.
3046  if ( (longDouble_value != longDouble_value) || (longDouble_value == std::numeric_limits<long double>::quiet_NaN()) )
3047  {
3048  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<long double>::quiet_NaN()";
3049  curprint ( "__builtin_nanl (\"\")");
3050  }
3051  else
3052  {
3053  if (longDouble_value == std::numeric_limits<long double>::signaling_NaN())
3054  {
3055  // curprint ( "std::numeric_limits<long double>::signaling_NaN()";
3056  curprint ( "__builtin_nansl (\"\")");
3057  }
3058  else
3059  {
3060  // typical case!
3061  // curprint ( longdbl_val->get_value();
3062  // AS (11/08/2005) add support for values as string
3063  if (longdbl_val->get_valueString() == "") {
3064  curprint ( tostring(longDouble_value) );
3065  if (!info.get_user_defined_literal()) {
3066  curprint ( "L" );
3067  }
3068  } else {
3069  std::string strVal = longdbl_val->get_valueString();
3070  if (info.get_user_defined_literal() && ( strVal.at(strVal.length() - 1) == 'l' || strVal.at(strVal.length() - 1) == 'L' ) ) {
3071  strVal = strVal.substr(0, strVal.length() - 1);
3072  }
3073  curprint (strVal);
3074  }
3075  }
3076  }

3120 void
3121 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTypeTraitBuiltinOperator(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info)
3122  {
3123  SgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator* operatorExp = isSgTypeTraitBuiltinOperator(expr);
3124  ASSERT_not_null(operatorExp);
3125 
3126  string functionNameString = operatorExp->get_name();
3127  curprint(functionNameString);
3128 
3129  ROSE_ASSERT(operatorExp->get_args().empty() == false);
3130 
3131  SgNodePtrList& list = operatorExp->get_args();
3132  SgNodePtrList::iterator operand = list.begin();
3133  curprint("(");
3134  while (operand != list.end())
3135  {
3136  // DQ (4/24/2013): Moved this to be ahead so that the unparseArg value would be associated with the current argument.
3137  if (operand != list.begin())
3138  {
3139  curprint(",");
3140  }
3141 
3142  SgType* type = isSgType(*operand);
3143  SgExpression* expression = isSgExpression(*operand);
3144 
3145  // DQ (7/13/2013): Build a new SgUnparse_Info so that we can skip passing on any existing referenceNode for name qualification.
3146  // We need to debug name qualification seperately, if it is required, likely it could be fore any referenced types.
3147  SgUnparse_Info newinfo(info);
3148  newinfo.set_reference_node_for_qualification(operatorExp);
3149  ASSERT_not_null(newinfo.get_reference_node_for_qualification());
3150 
3151  if (type != NULL)
3152  {
3153  newinfo.set_SkipClassDefinition();
3154  newinfo.set_SkipEnumDefinition();
3155 
3156  newinfo.set_isTypeFirstPart();
3157  unp->u_type->unparseType(type, newinfo);
3158  newinfo.set_isTypeSecondPart();
3159  unp->u_type->unparseType(type, newinfo);
3160 
3161  newinfo.unset_isTypeFirstPart();
3162  newinfo.unset_isTypeSecondPart();
3163  }
3164  else
3165  {
3166  // DQ (3/24/2015): Added case of "__builtin_offsetof" to make it consistant with the change in the EDG/ROSE translation.
3167  // DQ (3/19/2015): For the case of the __offsetof() builtin function we have to avoid output of the structure (e.g. "(0*).field").
3168  if (functionNameString == "__offsetof" || functionNameString == "__builtin_offsetof")
3169  {
3170  // DQ (3/25/2015): Develop new way to supress output of "(0*)" in "(0*).field".
3171  // This is the more general form required for test2013_104.c "offsetof(zip_header_t, formatted.extra_len)".
3172  SgUnparse_Info info2(info);
3173  info2.set_skipCompilerGeneratedSubExpressions();
3174  ROSE_ASSERT(info2.skipCompilerGeneratedSubExpressions() == true);
3175 
3176  unparseExpression(expression,info2);
3177  }
3178  else
3179  {
3180  unparseExpression(expression,info);
3181  }
3182  }
3183  operand++;
3184  }
3185  curprint(")");
3186  }

3190 // void Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseFuncCall
3191 //
3192 // This function is called whenever we unparse a function call. It is divided up
3193 // into two parts. The first part unparses the function call and its arguments
3194 // using an "in-order" tree traversal method. This is done when we have a binary
3195 // operator overloading function and the operator overloading option is turned off.
3196 // The second part unparses the function call directly in a list-like manner. This
3197 // is done for non-operator function calls, or when the operator overloading option
3198 // is turned on.

3997 #endif
3998  }

5190 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparsePseudoDtorRef(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info & info)
5191  {
5192  SgPseudoDestructorRefExp* pdre = isSgPseudoDestructorRefExp(expr);
5193  ASSERT_not_null(pdre);
5194 
5195  SgType *objt = pdre->get_object_type();
5196  SgNamedType* namedType = isSgNamedType(objt);
5197  if (namedType != NULL)
5198  {
5199 
5200  // DQ (1/18/2020): Adding support for name qualification (see Cxx11_tests/test2020_56.C).
5201  SgName nameQualifier = pdre->get_qualified_name_prefix();
5202  if (nameQualifier.is_null() == false)
5203  {
5204  SgName nameOfType = namedType->get_name();
5205  SgName name = nameQualifier + nameOfType + "::";
5206  curprint(name.str());
5207  }
5208  curprint("~");
5209  curprint(namedType->get_name().str());
5210 
5211  // DQ (3/14/2012): Note that I had to add this for the case of EDG 4.3, but it was not required previously for EDG 3.3, something in ROSE has likely changed.
5212  curprint("()");
5213  }
5214  else
5215  {
5216  curprint("~");
5217 
5218  // DQ (3/14/2012): This is the case of of a primative type (e.g. "~int"), which is allowed.
5219  // PC: I do not think this case will ever occur in practice. If it does, the resulting
5220  // code will be invalid. It may, however, appear in an implicit template instantiation.
5221  unp->u_type->unparseType(objt, info);
5222  }
5223  }

5226 void Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseCudaKernelCall(SgExpression* expr, SgUnparse_Info& info) {
5227 
5228  SgCudaKernelCallExp* kernel_call = isSgCudaKernelCallExp(expr);
5229  ASSERT_not_null(kernel_call);
5230 
5231  unparseExpression(kernel_call->get_function(), info);
5232 
5233  SgCudaKernelExecConfig * exec_config = isSgCudaKernelExecConfig(kernel_call->get_exec_config());
5234  ASSERT_not_null(exec_config);
5235 
5236  curprint ("<<<");
5237 
5238  SgExpression * grid_exp = exec_config->get_grid();
5239  ASSERT_not_null(grid_exp);
5240  unparseExpression(grid_exp, info);
5241  curprint (",");
5242 
5243  SgExpression * blocks_exp = exec_config->get_blocks();
5244  ASSERT_not_null(blocks_exp);
5245  unparseExpression(blocks_exp, info);
5246 
5247  SgExpression * shared_exp = exec_config->get_shared();
5248  if (shared_exp != NULL) {
5249  curprint (",");
5250  unparseExpression(shared_exp, info);
5251 
5252  SgExpression * stream_exp = exec_config->get_stream();
5253  if (stream_exp != NULL) {
5254  curprint (",");
5255  unparseExpression(stream_exp, info);
5256  }
5257  }
5258 
5259  curprint (">>>");
5260 
5261  curprint ( "(");
5262  if ( kernel_call->get_args() != NULL) {
5263  SgExpressionPtrList& list = kernel_call->get_args()->get_expressions();
5264  SgExpressionPtrList::iterator arg = list.begin();
5265  while (arg != list.end()) {
5266  unparseExpression((*arg), info);
5267  arg++;
5268  if (arg != list.end())
5269  curprint ( ",");
5270  }
5271  }
5272  curprint ( ")");
5273 }
